tasks.title: Developer API Key Vault — Schema, Service & Dashboard Route
tasks.objective: Implement the Developer API Key Vault feature enabling developers to generate, list, revoke, and manage HMAC-SHA256-signed API keys with prefix 'aroh_live_' (production) and 'aroh_test_' (test). Keys must be tier-gated (Basic: 60 rpm, Pro: 300 rpm, Enterprise: 1200 rpm). Implement the /dashboard/keys route, the key management Zod schema in @aroh/asdk, the server-side generation service, and Firestore persistence layer.
prohibited_scope: Products/ files (zero modifications)
Modifying existing schema types in ways that break existing 239 tests
Storing raw API key values in plaintext Firestore documents
Implementing client-side key generation or balance logic
Creating speculative spoke adapter capsules
Implementing Wave 2 Task 02 (Webhook) prematurely
security_requirements: HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens using Node.js crypto module
Key prefix must distinguish aroh_live_ (production) and aroh_test_ (test/sandbox)
Store only key hash (SHA-256) in Firestore — never the raw key value
Key is shown exactly once upon creation; subsequent reads return masked form
Tier-gated rate limits enforced server-side: Basic 60rpm, Pro 300rpm, Enterprise 1200rpm
Authorization: only authenticated user can manage their own keys
Key revocation must be irreversible within same request (no undelete)
API routes must use Zod schema validation on all inputs
expected_tests: npm test in Aroh (239+ assertions, all passing)
tasks.expected_commit: feat(developer): implement API key vault schema, service, and dashboard route [Wave 2 Task 1]
tasks.rollback_checkpoint: Create a git stash or tag before starting implementation: git tag WAVE-02-TASK-01-START
external_side_effects: Firestore: new developer_api_keys collection (creation only, no deletion of existing data)
tasks.resume_condition: If blocked, stash all work, record WAVE-02-TASK-01-BLOCKED handoff, and continue only if Task 02 is independently executable

tasks.title: Asynchronous Webhook Clearance Engine
tasks.objective: Implement the Asynchronous Webhook Clearance Engine enabling developers to register webhook endpoints and receive signed event notifications for platform events. Implement: webhook endpoint registration schema and CRUD, event dispatcher with HMAC-SHA256 signature header (x-aroh-signature), exponential backoff retry (3 attempts, 2^n * 500ms), and the four initial event types: aros.credited, aros.debited, membership.upgraded, challenge.completed.
prerequisites: WAVE-02-TASK-01 completed and verified (API Key Vault must exist as the developer identity and auth layer)
prohibited_scope: Products/ files (zero modifications)
Implementing a real background job queue (use in-process queue stub for now)
Making real outbound HTTP calls to external webhook endpoints in tests
Implementing Task 03 (Fiat On-Ramp) prematurely
security_requirements: Each webhook delivery signed with HMAC-SHA256 using developer's API key secret as the signing key
Signature delivered in x-aroh-signature header in format: sha256=<hex>
Retry policy: exponential backoff, max 3 attempts, delay = 2^attempt * 500ms
Events must include: type, version, timestamp, source, entity_ref, payload, correlation_id
Events must not contain secrets or sensitive PII beyond required entity reference
Webhook URLs must be validated as HTTPS-only (no plaintext HTTP)
Webhook endpoint must be user-owned: only the registering developer can delete or list
expected_tests: npm test in Aroh (all previous assertions + new webhook tests, all passing)
tasks.expected_commit: feat(developer): implement async webhook clearance engine [Wave 2 Task 2]
external_side_effects: NOTE: Outbound webhook dispatch is stubbed in test mode; no real HTTP calls made during tests
tasks.resume_condition: If blocked on TASK-01 dependency, enter BLOCKED state and stop

tasks.title: Fiat-to-Aros Settlement On-Ramp (Stripe Checkout)
tasks.objective: Implement the Fiat-to-Aros Settlement On-Ramp enabling users to purchase Aros tokens via Stripe Checkout sessions using Next.js server actions. Conversion rate: $1.00 USD = 100 Aros. The settlement must use the immutable Aros ledger service (no direct balance writes), and Stripe webhook events must be processed through the Webhook Clearance Engine (WAVE-02-TASK-02).
prerequisites: WAVE-02-TASK-02 completed (Webhook Clearance Engine — Stripe webhook events use it)
prohibited_scope: Products/ files (zero modifications)
Direct Firestore balance writes (must use ledger transaction records)
Hard-coding Stripe keys in source files (must use environment variables)
Implementing real Stripe API calls in test environment (use mock Stripe mode)
Implementing Phase 3.5 tasks prematurely
security_requirements: Stripe secret key must only exist in server-side environment variables (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY)
Stripe webhook secret must be used to validate all incoming Stripe webhook events (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
Conversion rate ($1.00 = 100 Aros) must be enforced server-side only
Idempotency: Stripe payment_intent or charge ID used as deduplication key to prevent double-crediting
D2 Aros Execution flow: Authenticate → Authorize → Validate → Idempotency Check → Atomic Economic Operation → Persist → Verify → Event → Response
expected_tests: npm test in Aroh (all previous assertions + new payment tests, all passing)
tasks.expected_commit: feat(payment): implement fiat-to-aros settlement on-ramp via Stripe Checkout [Wave 2 Task 3]
external_side_effects: Stripe: requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env vars (BLOCKED if not present, report as EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY_MISSING)
Firestore: new payment_intents collection for idempotency tracking
tasks.resume_condition: If Stripe env vars are absent, create WAVE-02-TASK-03-BLOCKED handoff citing EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY_MISSING and proceed to TASK-04 if it is independent

tasks.title: W3C Distributed Tracing — traceparent Propagation (Phase 3.5)
tasks.objective: Propagate W3C traceparent headers across all AROH Next.js API routes and spoke adapter integrations, enabling distributed tracing correlation between the platform hub and external services. Implement a lightweight tracing utility in @aroh/asdk that generates and validates W3C trace context. Middleware must extract or generate traceparent on ingress and attach to all outbound requests.
prohibited_scope: Products/ files (zero modifications)
Adding external observability vendor SDKs (OpenTelemetry collectors, Datadog, etc.) unless authorized
Modifying existing API route business logic (only add tracing header injection)
Implementing Phase 3.5 Task 2 (WebSocket metrics) prematurely
security_requirements: traceparent header must be validated on ingress (malformed values must be replaced, not propagated)
Trace IDs must not contain sensitive user data
Tracing must not log request bodies or secrets
expected_tests: npm test in Aroh (all previous assertions + new tracing tests, all passing)
tasks.expected_commit: feat(observability): implement W3C traceparent propagation across API routes [Wave 2 Task 4]
tasks.resume_condition: Independent of Task 03 (Stripe). Can execute if Tasks 01 and 02 complete.

tasks.title: Real-Time Operational Telemetry Broker — WebSocket Metrics Stream (Phase 3.5)
tasks.objective: Implement a WebSocket-based real-time operational telemetry metrics stream in the /admin route, displaying settlement latency and active user journeys. The metrics broker must consume events from the Aros ledger (WAVE-02-TASK-01 keys layer) and the Webhook Clearance Engine dispatcher (WAVE-02-TASK-02).
prohibited_scope: Products/ files (zero modifications)
Modifying core Aros ledger transaction logic
Using external real-time services (Pusher, Ably, etc.) unless explicitly authorized
Starting Phase 4 / Wave 3 tasks
security_requirements: WebSocket endpoint must require authenticated session
Admin route must enforce role: admin or operator
Metrics stream must not expose individual user wallet balances or PII
expected_tests: npm test in Aroh (all previous assertions + new telemetry tests, all passing)
tasks.expected_commit: feat(telemetry): implement real-time WebSocket operational metrics broker [Wave 2 Task 5]
tasks.resume_condition: Blocked if TASK-04 not complete (requires traceparent for correlation). Enter WAVE-02-TASK-05-BLOCKED if dependencies not met.

stop_boundary: After WAVE-02-TASK-05 is committed, pushed, and verified, execute Wave 2 Completion Gate and STOP. Do not begin Phase 4 or Wave 3.
